What Works:
-Halo-ish
-Gameplay (Portals, guns around the map, shooting etc.)
-Easy game to run
-Better than average free to play
-Casual and Ranked
-Skins and customization

What Doesn't:
-Can't pick a game mode in casual and ranked
-No training area to get better
-Few game modes
-Bots in casual
-Ranked doesn't match others with your skill

Verdict: For a free to play game, this is amazing. The shooting experience is great, fun to play with friends and have a laugh while destroying some plebs. Resemblance to Halo. Would definitely recommend. Overall: 8/10

The more you play this game, the more you realize how badly it was made. Aim means nothing when all you have to do is portal around the map like there's no tomorrow and spray in your enemies general direction. Maps are beyond boring, the pre-match "lobby" is annoying as fuck, the weapons are subpar, the game modes are bland and stale. Don't waste your time with this unless you're broke and can't be helped to find a job to buy a better game. Have barely any hope whatsoever for the sequel since this game has been a steaming pile of garbage since it released.

It's a good game. I can't fault it in that regard. It's fun, the portals are extremely fun to use and it has overall some of the nicest and most responsive gun play in any game I've played.

Despite that I can't in good consciousness recommend it in the current state. The playerbase is so low you're guaranteed multiple bots in every single game. Varies massively by game. Sometimes they're so good you're unable to compete, firing at you ahead of times from positions where they can't have possibly known you were there, such as being way out of range of where you'd show up on the minimap or hear footsteps and yet pre-firing the corner despite that. Sometimes it's the exact opposite - I've had multiple games, specifically modes like Contamination, where you can be stood completely still in an open area and despite that the bots will just run around in circles and not even try to find you, or they'll just run in a straight like directly towards you. Every game is one or the other with no in-between and when it's at least half the players in every single game, no amount of well-designed mechanics can save it.

Splitgate is a great first person portal shooter with amazing halo- like combat i have played 16.8 hours as of writing this review and have just gotten into ranked and am have a great time with the competitive challenge that now comes with the game. i would definitely recommend it to any halo fan and think that you will have a great time with it

It's a beautiful mix of Quake, Halo and Portal. Absolutely incredibly fun.
It's free, and at worst you'll lose some time.
For your first profile levels your matches will be against bots, which aren't marked as bots on the scoreboards, so that's a bit sketch, but that's honestly the only minus I can really give this game.
The movement, the gunplay, the fact that there's a mode called Teabag Confirmed, and the general vibe of the game is awesome.
Since it's an F2P game, there's MTX, as one would expect. However, they're all cosmetics, so it's completely okay by me.
So yeah, give it a shot, and teabag some nerds out there.

It's astonishing how original Splitgate feels, despite how virtually every aspect is taken from other games. The maps and guns feel straight from Halo 2 or 3; the TTK feels a lot like Destiny 1; you have access to the jetpack from Tribes; you get portals from Portal; all the binding, peripheral elements harken directly to Unreal.
